audit.why: 54.85% WR over 1670 games — Taliyah-favored but execution-heavy (Wind Wall, dash taxing); TRICKY 7/10 is defensible though arguably a shade high.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full chart was blanket 'Skill' rows 0-5 with Yasuo at row 6; content and packet both say Taliyah 0-3, Skill at 6, Yasuo at first item, Taliyah 2+ items. Full row 5 and 6 were both wrong vs the other layer.
audit.why: Kit-supported: her range owns pre-item lane, his first crit item plus wave resets is his spike, her E mines tax his dash-reliant late all-in.
audit.corrected: Full sides aligned to content; whys rewritten per row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly calls the W-E result a 'root' (Unraveled Earth stuns). Content and full claim Wind Wall blocks 'your Q and E' — E is a ground minefield with no projectile flag; only Q and W are blockable. Missing interaction: Way of the Wanderer shield absorbs the burst opener — never stated. Wind Wall cooldown (25s rank 1 / 17 max, 4s duration) absent everywhere.
audit.why: Taliyah kit: E has no projectile flag, mines 'explode and stun'; Yasuo kit: P shield, W 25/23/21/19/17.
audit.corrected: root→stun in five fields; Q-and-E claim narrowed to Q; shield-strip and Wind Wall numbers added to report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; dosFull[2].d said 'fifteen-second invitation' for a 25-17s Wind Wall.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in both fields.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It governs your forward steps. - W Seismic Shove spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1, 17 at max, and blocks projectiles for 4s — bait it with one rock, then trade in the gap. - His passive shield refills as he moves: strip it before you burst. - Your 14s W spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q from fresh ground on his last-hit, and if he steps to answer, W-shove him across the E-field — the full geometry trade is half a health bar.
edits.after: His EQ3 needs a dash through your minefield — W him mid-dash and the mines stun him instead; the whole combo dies to one displacement.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — its 25-second cooldown is your invite.

edits.before: Trading while standing on your own Worked Ground — one-stone Qs lose every exchange your positioning already conceded.
edits.after: Once the mines expire his dashes are free — extended trades favor his 4s Steel Tempest over your mana bar every time.

edits.before: Track Yasuo’s Wind Wall: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks your Q and W rocks for 4 seconds but not your E mines — and his passive shield eats poke: strip it, then trade.

edits.after: Flash + Teleport or Ignite — TP extends the roam plan cross-map; Ignite converts the W-E burst into early deletions. Pick by how hard you intend to roam.

edits.before: You have the range and wave control on Yasuo early. Threaded Volley shoves fast and zones his Sweeping Blade approach, and your poke out-distances Steel Tempest, so make him take chip damage every time he steps up. His Wind Wall blocks your Q and E, so bait it with a single rock first, then land your real poke and W-E combo once it's on cooldown; a clean root out of dash range is his worst nightmare.
edits.after: You have the range and wave control on Yasuo early. Threaded Volley shoves fast and zones his Sweeping Blade approach, and your poke out-distances Steel Tempest, so make him take chip damage every time he steps up. His Wind Wall blocks your Q rocks, so bait it with a single rock first, then land your real poke and W-E combo once it's on cooldown; a clean stun out of dash range is his worst nightmare.

edits.before: Yasuo's first crit item is his spike: Sweeping Blade resets off your wave let him dash past your poke and Wind Wall the follow-up, so respect that window and don't get caught without W. After it, the lane swings back to you: E minefield zones his dash lanes and a W-E timed through his expired Wind Wall roots him out of his own all-in. Keep him at range, punish whiffed dashes, and never poke into an active wall.
